key_insight: Embedding an asymptotic boundary-layer corrector in neural trial functions preserves accuracy at small viscosity without a grid that resolves the thin vorticity layer.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce the cost of viscosity-robust flow simulation by representing near-wall layers analytically rather than refining the residual grid.
method: Use a singular-layer PINN for 2D incompressible flow in vorticity–stream function form with slip boundary conditions.
Tie the analytical corrector’s amplitude to the network’s wall trace, avoiding prior knowledge of the limit solution.
Replace the residual Laplacian with coarse-grid finite-volume flux differences to obtain sl-FVNN.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports viscosity-uniform errors over six decades for Stokes and Navier–Stokes tests, with sl-FVNN matching sl-PINN accuracy within seed scatter at about half the training-step cost.
watch_item: The demonstrated setting uses 2D slip-wall flows; extending it to other boundary conditions or geometries may require new asymptotic correctors.
paper_title: Singular layer neural networks for the Navier-Stokes equations at small viscosity
